newsitem.title: JAPAN: OTC index rebounds after 15 sessions of losses.
newsitem.headline: OTC index rebounds after 15 sessions of losses.

text.p: Japan's over-the-counter (OTC) index ended with gains on Wednesday for the first time since the 1997 business year started April 1, when bargain hunting emerged to provide some support to the sector.
"Trade is still very slow as investors are sidelined, but some shares have shed so much, they are finally beginning to look attractive," a "Big Four" broker said.
The OTC index ended 1.37 points or 0.13 percent higher at 1.033.86, halting a slide of 15 consecutive sessions of losses.
The index, which covers mainly smaller domestic companies, has tumbled some 75 percent from the record high of 4,149.20 set on July 9, 1990.
But an official at Ichiyoshi Securities Co Ltd, a brokerage specialising in OTC and small shares, said that the rise was likely to be temporary.

"Foreign investors were net buyers of OTC stocks in the last week of March and the first week of April, and there were some private investors today, but all were after bargains only, with fast profits in mind," he said.

Brokers attributed the feeble state of the market to a host of factors ranging from the stagnant state of the overall market, lack of registrations by firms with the potential of leading the market, as well as a hesitant recovery in the economy.
"The atmosphere is not very encouraging for investors at the moment as there are too many uncertainties," an analyst at a foreign brokerage said.
